_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 directly to contract v3, mirroring the Boston exemplar (phase3/boston-fleet-investors.json) per GROK-SPEC-archetype-templates-2026-08-15.md + ADDENDUM v3. Sources: san-diego/REVENUE-STACK-SAN-DIEGO.md + san-diego/CREW-COST-SAN-DIEGO.md + san-diego/SPEED-RULES-SAN-DIEGO.md + san-diego/hub.json (version 2026-08-15-san-diego-v1). CONTRACT v3: only `title` (≤6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (≤140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. Fleet financing only — the equity/fundraise/defense/Gulf content firewalls in FLEET-INVESTORS-BRIEF.md §5 apply in full. D6′ utilization-stack economics lead frame; upside rows are never summed into base totals. OMISSIONS (fail closed): `fleet_phasing` omitted — no sourced per-line fleet counts or launch/full-build capital plan exists for San Diego this pass; `asset` top-level key omitted — it was a Boston v2 provenance artifact, superseded by navier_intro. SAN DIEGO HONESTY LOCK: mid case ~8.5-yr payback is the headline; conservative is cash-negative and renders a neutral '—' payback with fn8; seat pricing is DERIVED (status modeled + fn7), not canon and not market-tested; the year-round experiences market carries visible narrative weight per REVENUE-STACK §1/§5.

fn1.text: Experience, charter and comparator fares are benchmarked to San Diego operators' published 2026 prices.

fn2.text: Demand figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — not commitments or commercial relationships.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times respect posted bay speed limits. The Port Code itself (§4.30(c)3) applies prudent speed, not the 5 mph cap, in the marked Chula Vista Harbor Channel; schedules here keep the 5 mph assumption until the Port confirms how that applies to foilborne transit.

fn5.text: Crew costs are benchmarked to published San Diego-area wage data with a buffer for wage growth to 2026; shift structure to be confirmed in an operations walkthrough.
fn5._provenance: Crew costs are benchmarked to published San Diego-area wage data (BLS metro means) with a buffer for wage growth to 2026; shift structure to be confirmed in an operations walkthrough. · BLS OEWS San Diego metro means; see handoff/archetypes/san-diego/CREW-COST-SAN-DIEGO.md

fn6.text: Spot-seat legs apply each scenario's stated fill rate (10–30%) to residual commute capacity after guaranteed seats; subtotals rounded to the nearest dollar.

fn7.text: Commuter pricing is derived, not market-tested: the $650–850 seat-month band and $25–35 spot fares are built from the bay's own benchmarks — the $15 public ferry on the flagship pair, a ~$29 average ride-hail, the $72 MTS monthly pass, and $120–280 monthly parking — with industry pass-discount structure applied.

fn8.text: The conservative case is cash-negative at derived seat prices and deliberately punitive fills; it is shown for honesty and is not financeable.

copy.subline: One vessel, four revenue layers. In San Diego the commuter layer builds slowly against low public fares — and a deep, year-round experience market carries more of the payback.
copy.small_print: Indicative economics — conservative defaults, ranges not points. Seat pricing is derived, not market-tested.

copy.headline: One asset. One day. Four demand layers.
copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in ~15% of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole day. San Diego's low public fares make the commuter seat build deliberate; its year-round experience market — daily harbor sailings, a Dec–Apr whale season, two on-network convention centers — carries more of the payback here.

revenue_rows.note: A derived monthly pass band — priced against the bay's $15 ferry, ~$29 ride-hail average and $72 transit pass.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil, not a boat with a battery.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 20 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the chop for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional boats. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

tech_chips.label: Energy
tech_chips.value: up to ~90% less than a planing hull

copy.note: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market — the 7-city network is the residual-value story.
